bibl.title: Integrated analysis of multimodal single-cell data

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: cells measured two ways at once - transcriptome plus surface protein, or plus chromatin accessibility - and the problem of deciding which measurement to believe
span.quote: Even within the same dataset, the relative utility of each modality to define cell states may vary across individual cells.

span.label: how to combine several simultaneous measurements of one cell into a single definition of its state, without being told in advance which measurement matters
span.quote: Here, we introduce “weighted-nearest neighbor” analysis, an unsupervised framework to learn the relative utility of each data type in each cell, enabling an integrative analysis of multiple modalities.

span.label: weighted-nearest-neighbor analysis: a per-cell, unsupervised weight for each modality, plus a 211,000-cell multimodal reference atlas and a way to map new datasets onto it
span.quote: Our approach represents a broadly applicable strategy to analyze single-cell multimodal datasets and to look beyond the transcriptome toward a unified and multimodal definition of cellular identity.

span.label: method
span.quote: Our approach consists of four broad steps, as explained in detail below: (1) Constructing independent _k_-nearest neighbor (KNN) graphs for both modalities. (2) Performing within and across-modality prediction (3) Calculating cell-specific modality weights. (4) Calculating a WNN graph.

span.label: cell states that one measurement type cannot separate and another can - CD4 and CD8 T cells blend in the transcriptome and separate in protein; dendritic cells do the reverse
span.quote: Although established technologies like single-cell RNA-seq (scRNA-seq) are capable of discovering new cell types and states in heterogeneous tissues, transcriptomics alone is often incapable of separating molecularly similar, but functionally distinct, categories of immune cells.

span.label: build a k-nearest-neighbour graph per modality, predict each cell from its neighbours within and across modalities, turn the relative accuracy of those predictions into per-cell weights by a softmax, and build one graph from the weighted combination
span.term: build a k-nearest-neighbour graph per modality, predict each cell from its neighbours within and across modalities, turn the relative accuracy of those predictions into per-cell weights by a softmax, and build one graph from the weighted combination
span.quote: We provide a detailed mathematical description for each component of the WNN workflow in the STAR Methods, highlighting three key steps: (1) obtaining within modality and cross-modality predictions, (2) converting these to prediction affinities, based on a cell-specific bandwidth kernel, and (3) calculating modality weights using a softmax transformation.

span.label: the core move: if a cell's neighbours in one modality predict its measured profile well, that modality is capturing its state; if they predict badly, it is not. The weight is the ratio of those two accuracies
span.term: prediction accuracy as evidence of informativeness
span.quote: Next, we independently averaged the molecular profiles of protein neighbors and RNA neighbors (i.e., predicted the molecular contents of a cell from its neighbors), and compared the averages to their original measured values.

span.label: why rare cells are not penalised: a fixed neighbour count for the kernel bandwidth would hold common and rare states to the same scale, so the bandwidth is set from the 20 cells with the LOWEST non-zero Jaccard similarity - similar enough to matter, unlikely to be the same state
span.quote: For each cell , we therefore aim to identify the 20 cells in the dataset with the _lowest_ non-zero Jaccard similarity. We expect that these represent cells that exhibit some similarity with cell , but are unlikely to reside in the same molecular state.

span.label: how a spurious edge is told from a real one - the Jaccard metric counts shared nearest neighbours, so local density separates well-supported links from coincidental similarity
span.quote: However, it is possible to identify these spurious edges through the use of the Jaccard metric. This identifies the number of shared nearest neighbors between two cells, thereby exploiting the local density of each data point to separate well-supported from spurious edges.

span.label: what the weighting buys: one data type is allowed to make up for another's weakness, cell by cell, so the combined analysis is not limited by whichever measurement happens to be poor for that cell
span.quote: We confirmed that our results were robust to a range of values for _k_ ( Figure S2), and the incorporation of protein information in the WNN graph does not come at the expense of identifying transcriptomically congruent neighborhoods

span.label: WNN needs a dimensional reduction to describe neighbourhood structure, so it does not work on categorical or low-dimensional data
span.quote: First, WNN requires a dimensional reduction to describe the neighborhood structure between cells. This requirement is not compatible with categorical or low-dimensional data.

span.label: IT ASSUMES THE MODALITIES DO NOT DEFINE CONFLICTING SETS OF CELL STATES - and the authors say the assumption may be problematic when integrating morphological, functional and molecular data. An integration method whose premise is that its inputs agree
span.quote: Second, WNN assumes that modalities do not define conflicting sets of cell states. Although we have not observed this when using molecular data such as chromatin state, gene expression, and surface protein abundance, this assumption may be problematic when integrating morphological, functional, and molecular data.

span.label: the atlas is built from peripheral blood mononuclear cells, so it contains almost no erythrocytes or granulocytes - and any query containing them will have nowhere to map them
span.quote: In addition, our circulating immune atlas was constructed from PBMCs and therefore contains few cells with no nuclei (erythrocytes) or multi-lobed nuclei (granulocytes).

span.label: demonstrated on exactly that: neutrophil populations present in a COVID-19 query and absent from the reference could not be mapped
span.quote: Notably, populations of developing and differentiated neutrophils, which were identified by the original manuscript as being uniquely present in COVID-19 samples but were absent from our reference, could not be successfully mapped

span.label: the enrichment panels achieve high fold-enrichment and still cannot sort a truly homogeneous population - the precision and recall figures are published alongside the enrichment ones
span.quote: We show precision and recall metrics for each panel in Figure S4, demonstrating that it remains challenging to sort truly “homogeneous” populations of high-resolution subsets using a small number of markers.

span.label: heterogeneity in monocyte inflammatory genes was left undivided BECAUSE it varied across volunteers - a cluster the authors declined to call a cell state
span.quote: We also identified substantial heterogeneity in the expression of inflammatory genes such as _IL1B_ and _CCL3_ within monocyte populations, but because this heterogeneity varied across different volunteers, we conservatively did not further subdivide these states

span.label: adding increasing amounts of random Gaussian noise to the protein data, to mimic nonspecific antibody binding, and watching what the learned weights do
span.note: eliminates: the modality weights being an artefact of the method rather than a measurement of information content - THE WEIGHTS FELL DOSE-DEPENDENTLY AND REACHED ZERO, which is the behaviour the method claims and could have failed to show · outcome: held
span.quote: We confirmed this using a simulation experiment, where we added increasing amounts of random Gaussian noise to the ADT data, in order to mimic increases in nonspecific binding

span.label: calculating the modality weights with no knowledge of cell-type labels, then checking whether they line up with known biology
span.note: eliminates: the weights being read off the answer - CD8 T cells got high protein weights and dendritic cells high RNA weights, and the labels were not available to the calculation · outcome: held
span.quote: We observed that cells classified as CD8+ T cells were assigned higher protein modality weights, whereas DCs were assigned higher RNA modality weights, recapitulating our biological expectations despite the fact that the calculation of modality weights was unsupervised and unaware of cell-type labels

span.label: counting incorrect CD8/CD4 edges in each graph as a hard number rather than judging the UMAP pictures
span.note: eliminates: a visual impression of better separation standing in for a measurement - 944 wrong edges in RNA, 12 in protein, 20 in the combined graph · outcome: held
span.quote: We found that for CD8+ T cells, the most similar RNA neighbors often reflected a mix of CD8+ and CD4+ T cells (in the RNA KNN graph, there are a total of 944 incorrect edges that connect CD8+ to CD4+ T cells). By contrast, protein neighbors were predominantly correctly identified as CD8+ T cells (in the protein KNN graph, 12 CD8+/CD4+ edges were identified).

span.label: varying k from 10 to 50 and re-running the whole procedure
span.note: eliminates: the result depending on the neighbourhood size, which is the one free parameter a reader would suspect first · outcome: held
span.quote: We confirmed that our results were robust to a range of values for _k_ ( Figure S2), and the incorporation of protein information in the WNN graph does not come at the expense of identifying transcriptomically congruent neighborhoods

span.label: benchmarking against two named alternative methods, totalVI and MOFA+, on a stated metric - how well each integrated space reconstructs a cell's molecular state from its neighbours
span.note: eliminates: `our method is better` resting on the authors' own preferred view of the output; the metric is declared before the comparison and applies equally to all three · outcome: held
span.quote: We reasoned that we could quantify the performance of the different methods by comparing the similarity of each cell’s molecular state to its closest neighbors in the integrated latent space.

span.label: HOLDING THE QUERY DATASET'S PROTEIN MEASUREMENTS OUT of the reference mapping, then using them to check the annotations the transcriptome alone produced
span.note: eliminates: the mapping being scored on the data it was given - the protein data is a true held-out test, and the predicted cell types carried the protein markers they should · outcome: held
span.quote: We verified the accuracy of our predictions using the query protein data, which was held out of the reference mapping procedure, yet revealed expression patterns based on our predicted annotations that were fully concordant with our reference dataset.

span.label: validating a computational prediction on a different instrument - CyTOF on the original samples plus 16 more, against the scRNA-seq-predicted MAIT abundance
span.note: eliminates: a depletion that exists only in the pipeline; the correlation between the two methods was 0.911 and the CyTOF cohort reproduced the depletion independently · outcome: held
span.quote: To validate our findings, we performed CyTOF on both the original samples and a validation cohort of 16 additional samples. We observed strong quantitative agreement (R = 0.911) in the fraction of MAIT cells predicted by scRNA-seq and measured by CyTOF in the original cohort

span.label: sorting cells by the predicted marker panels and sequencing them in bulk, using THE EXACT ANTIBODY CLONES from the CITE-seq panel
span.note: eliminates: a discrepancy between the two assays caused by different antibodies binding different epitopes - the authors name this as the reason for using the same clones · outcome: held
span.quote: For this population, as well as a subgroup of highly cytotoxic CD8+ T cells (CD8\_TEM\_5), we successfully validated our enrichment panels in an independent set of PBMCs from healthy donors by conventional flow cytometry followed by bulk RNA-seq

span.label: modality weights
span.quote: The RNA and protein modality weights are non-negative, unique to each cell, and sum to 1.

span.label: modalities
span.quote: Here, we introduce “weighted-nearest neighbor” analysis, an unsupervised framework to learn the relative utility of each data type in each cell, enabling an integrative analysis of multiple modalities.

span.label: spurious edges
span.quote: Recent work has clearly demonstrated that KNN-graphs are prone to the formation of spurious edges, which represent links between cells that share some similarity molecular profiles, but are not in a matched molecular state

span.label: Jaccard metric
span.quote: However, it is possible to identify these spurious edges through the use of the Jaccard metric. This identifies the number of shared nearest neighbors between two cells, thereby exploiting the local density of each data point to separate well-supported from spurious edges.

span.label: cell states
span.quote: Even within the same dataset, the relative utility of each modality to define cell states may vary across individual cells.

span.label: transcriptome
span.quote: More broadly, this exhibits the challenge of defining cell states based on the transcriptome alone, because important sources of cellular heterogeneity may not correlate strongly with transcriptomic features despite being identifiable in other modalities.

span.label: scRNA-seq
span.quote: We found that the increasing ADT noise led to a decrease in protein weights for all cell types, in a dose-dependent manner. Moreover, protein modality weights were assigned to 0 after a sufficient amount of protein noise was added, correctly instructing downstream analyses to focus only on scRNA-seq data.

span.label: CITE-seq
span.quote: Notably, our flow cytometry experiments utilized the exact antibody clones represented in the CITE-seq experiment, which can help to ensure that the two assays will return concordant results.

span.label: CyTOF
span.quote: To validate our findings, we performed CyTOF on both the original samples and a validation cohort of 16 additional samples. We observed strong quantitative agreement (R = 0.911) in the fraction of MAIT cells predicted by scRNA-seq and measured by CyTOF in the original cohort

span.label: totalVI
span.quote: We next benchmarked WNN analysis against two recently introduced methods for multimodal integration: multi-omics factor analysis v2 (MOFA+) ( Argelaguet et al., 2020), which uses a statistical framework based on factor analysis, and totalVI ( Gayoso et al., 2019), which combines deep neural networks with a hierarchical Bayesian model.

span.label: sPCA
span.quote: Instead of seeking to identify a low-dimensional projection that maximizes total variance as in PCA, sPCA identifies a projection of the transcriptome dataset that maximally captures the structure defined in the WNN graph.

span.label: neutrophils
span.quote: Notably, populations of developing and differentiated neutrophils, which were identified by the original manuscript as being uniquely present in COVID-19 samples but were absent from our reference, could not be successfully mapped

span.label: modality weights → cell states
span.note: A NUMBER WHOSE MEANING IS UNDECIDED, AND THE PAPER SAYS SO. The weight is a proxy for the technical quality of a measurement AND may reflect the biological importance of that modality to the cell's identity. Those are different claims about different things and the same float carries both. There is no relation type for `this measure has two candidate interpretations and we cannot separate them` - the nearest available, `operationalised-as`, would pick one and hide the other
span.quote: Last, we note that the modality weights learned in our procedure serve not only as a proxy for the technical quality of a measurement type, but may also reflect the biological importance of each modality in determining cellular identity.

span.label: modalities → cell states
span.note: AN ASSUMPTION OF NON-CONFLICT, WHICH IS THE METHOD'S PREMISE AND ITS SECOND STATED LIMITATION. `WNN assumes that modalities do not define conflicting sets of cell states`, and the authors flag that the assumption may fail for morphological and functional data. Every one of the eight relation types asserts something HOLDS between two concepts; none can say `these two are assumed not to disagree, and the method has no behaviour if they do`
span.quote: Second, WNN assumes that modalities do not define conflicting sets of cell states. Although we have not observed this when using molecular data such as chromatin state, gene expression, and surface protein abundance, this assumption may be problematic when integrating morphological, functional, and molecular data.

span.label: modality weight - A PER-CELL NUMBER, NOT A PER-DATASET ONE, AND THE PAPER SAYS IT HAS TWO POSSIBLE MEANINGS. It is a proxy for the TECHNICAL QUALITY of a measurement in that cell, and it `may also reflect the BIOLOGICAL IMPORTANCE of each modality in determining cellular identity` - progenitors and differentiated cells came out with divergent weights. The same figure can mean `this instrument worked here` or `this axis is what this cell is`, and nothing in the number distinguishes them
span.quote: Last, we note that the modality weights learned in our procedure serve not only as a proxy for the technical quality of a measurement type, but may also reflect the biological importance of each modality in determining cellular identity.

span.label: weight, as computed here - EARNED BY A PREDICTION TEST, not assigned. Each cell is predicted from its neighbours within each modality and across them, the predictions are compared with the cell's actual measurements, and the RATIO of those accuracies becomes the weight after a softmax. Non-negative, unique to each cell, summing to 1
span.quote: The RNA and protein modality weights are non-negative, unique to each cell, and sum to 1.

span.label: unsupervised, of this procedure - MEANS UNAWARE OF CELL-TYPE LABELS, AND THAT IS WHAT MAKES THE AGREEMENT EVIDENCE. CD8 T cells got high protein weights and dendritic cells high RNA weights, `despite the fact that the calculation of modality weights was unsupervised and unaware of cell-type labels`. The recapitulation of a known biology is the check, and it only counts because the labels were withheld
span.quote: We observed that cells classified as CD8+ T cells were assigned higher protein modality weights, whereas DCs were assigned higher RNA modality weights, recapitulating our biological expectations despite the fact that the calculation of modality weights was unsupervised and unaware of cell-type labels

span.label: spurious edge - A LINK BETWEEN CELLS THAT RESEMBLE EACH OTHER WITHOUT BEING IN THE SAME STATE, and the paper counts them rather than describing them: 944 wrong CD8/CD4 edges in the RNA graph, 12 in the protein graph, 20 in the combined one. A quality claim with an integer behind it
span.quote: Recent work has clearly demonstrated that KNN-graphs are prone to the formation of spurious edges, which represent links between cells that share some similarity molecular profiles, but are not in a matched molecular state

span.label: annotation, in this atlas - THREE NESTED TIERS AND A CELL CARRIES ALL THREE. Level 1 has 8 categories, level 2 has 30, level 3 has 57. A result reported at one tier is not comparable with a result reported at another, and the granularity is a choice the reader has to make rather than one the data settles
span.quote: To assist in the interpretation of our clusters, we assign each cell three annotations with increasing granularity (level 1, 8 categories; level 2, 30 categories; level 3, 57 categories).

span.label: supervised, in `supervised principal component analysis` - SUPERVISED BY THE WNN GRAPH, NOT BY A HUMAN. sPCA finds the transcriptomic projection that best captures the structure the multimodal analysis already found, so the supervision comes from the other modality rather than from labels. `Supervised` and `unsupervised` are both used in this paper about the same pipeline, meaning different things
span.quote: Instead of seeking to identify a low-dimensional projection that maximizes total variance as in PCA, sPCA identifies a projection of the transcriptome dataset that maximally captures the structure defined in the WNN graph.

span.label: distinguishes-from → totalVI and MOFA+, two recently introduced multimodal integration methods based on deep neural networks with a hierarchical Bayesian model and on factor analysis respectively
span.quote: We next benchmarked WNN analysis against two recently introduced methods for multimodal integration: multi-omics factor analysis v2 (MOFA+) ( Argelaguet et al., 2020), which uses a statistical framework based on factor analysis, and totalVI ( Gayoso et al., 2019), which combines deep neural networks with a hierarchical Bayesian model.

span.label: distinguishes-from → scArches, a method for mapping single-cell RNA-seq queries onto reference datasets
span.quote: We benchmarked our method against scArches, a recently developed method for mapping scRNA-seq queries to reference datasets ( Lotfollahi et al., 2020) and observed that our approach yielded substantial improvements in accuracy and performance

span.label: critiques → the practice of defining cell states from the transcriptome alone, which cannot separate functionally distinct T cell populations however sensitive the technology
span.quote: Although established technologies like single-cell RNA-seq (scRNA-seq) are capable of discovering new cell types and states in heterogeneous tissues, transcriptomics alone is often incapable of separating molecularly similar, but functionally distinct, categories of immune cells.

span.label: extends → the unsupervised clustering analysis of Wilk et al.'s COVID-19 PBMC dataset, which found six T cell clusters where reference mapping resolved twelve
span.note: and the extension is not one-directional - the same comparison shows what the reference CANNOT do: neutrophils that the original unsupervised analysis found, because they were absent from the reference, could not be mapped at all
span.quote: Notably, populations of developing and differentiated neutrophils, which were identified by the original manuscript as being uniquely present in COVID-19 samples but were absent from our reference, could not be successfully mapped

span.label: builds-on → Barshan et al.'s supervised principal component analysis, applied here with the WNN graph as the supervising structure
span.quote: Instead of seeking to identify a low-dimensional projection that maximizes total variance as in PCA, sPCA identifies a projection of the transcriptome dataset that maximally captures the structure defined in the WNN graph.

span.label: scRNA-seq —causes→ spurious edges
span.note: direction on the measure: increases · strength of the relation: 0.85 — signed from a COUNT rather than from a hedge - 944 against 12 in the protein graph, on the same cells
span.quote: We found that for CD8+ T cells, the most similar RNA neighbors often reflected a mix of CD8+ and CD4+ T cells (in the RNA KNN graph, there are a total of 944 incorrect edges that connect CD8+ to CD4+ T cells). By contrast, protein neighbors were predominantly correctly identified as CD8+ T cells (in the protein KNN graph, 12 CD8+/CD4+ edges were identified).

span.label: modality weights —causes→ spurious edges
span.note: direction on the measure: reduces · strength of the relation: 0.85 — 20 against RNA's 944. The protein graph alone did better still at 12, which is why the claim is about ROBUSTNESS across cells rather than about beating every modality
span.quote: For example, the WNN graph contained only 20 CD8+/CD4+ edges.

span.label: transcriptome —contrasted-with→ modalities
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.8 — the paper's whole framing: the transcriptome is one modality among several and has been treated as the definition of cell state
span.quote: More broadly, this exhibits the challenge of defining cell states based on the transcriptome alone, because important sources of cellular heterogeneity may not correlate strongly with transcriptomic features despite being identifiable in other modalities.

span.label: CITE-seq —distinct-from→ CyTOF
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.9 — and the distinctness is what makes the agreement worth something - the MAIT depletion was found in one and confirmed in the other at R = 0.911
span.quote: We conclude that WNN analysis is capable of sensitively and robustly characterizing populations that cannot be identified by a single modality, exhibits best-in-class performance, and can be flexibly applied to multiple data types for integrative and multimodal analysis. ### A multimodal atlas of the human PBMCs Although flow cytometry and cytometry by time of flight (CyTOF) are widely used and powerful approaches for making high-dimensional measurements of protein expression in immune cells ( Bendall et al., 2011; Bodenmiller et al., 2012; Diggins et al., 2015; Saeys et al., 2016), CITE-seq’s use of distinct oligonucleotide barcode sequences provides a unique opportunity to profile very large panels of antibodies alongside cellular transcriptomes.

span.label: per-cell modality weights, learned unsupervised, recover known biology: CD8 T cells weight protein highly, dendritic cells weight RNA highly
span.quote: We observed that cells classified as CD8+ T cells were assigned higher protein modality weights, whereas DCs were assigned higher RNA modality weights, recapitulating our biological expectations despite the fact that the calculation of modality weights was unsupervised and unaware of cell-type labels

span.label: incorrect CD8/CD4 edges: 944 in the RNA graph, 12 in the protein graph, 20 in the weighted combination
span.quote: We found that for CD8+ T cells, the most similar RNA neighbors often reflected a mix of CD8+ and CD4+ T cells (in the RNA KNN graph, there are a total of 944 incorrect edges that connect CD8+ to CD4+ T cells). By contrast, protein neighbors were predominantly correctly identified as CD8+ T cells (in the protein KNN graph, 12 CD8+/CD4+ edges were identified).

span.label: adding Gaussian noise to the protein data drove protein weights down dose-dependently and to zero, correctly redirecting the analysis to RNA alone
span.quote: We found that the increasing ADT noise led to a decrease in protein weights for all cell types, in a dose-dependent manner. Moreover, protein modality weights were assigned to 0 after a sufficient amount of protein noise was added, correctly instructing downstream analyses to focus only on scRNA-seq data.

span.label: a 211,000-cell multimodal PBMC atlas from eight volunteers at three vaccination time points, resolving 57 clusters
span.quote: After NovaSeq sequencing, stringent quality control, and doublet filtration ( STAR Methods), our final dataset consists of 210,911 total cells and allows us to profile cellular heterogeneity in both the resting (unvaccinated) and activated (post-vaccination) immune system.

span.label: reference mapping found a MAIT-cell depletion in COVID-19 that unsupervised clustering had missed, confirmed by CyTOF at R = 0.911
span.quote: To validate our findings, we performed CyTOF on both the original samples and a validation cohort of 16 additional samples. We observed strong quantitative agreement (R = 0.911) in the fraction of MAIT cells predicted by scRNA-seq and measured by CyTOF in the original cohort

span.label: WNN matched or beat totalVI and MOFA+ on reconstructing each of 25 proteins from the integrated space
span.quote: We found that for each of the 25 proteins ( Figure 2 D), as well as the RNA transcriptome ( Figure S2), WNN analysis exhibited superior or equivalent performance to alternative approaches.

span.label: modality weights = per-cell values reflecting the relative information content of each data type in that cell; non-negative, unique per cell, summing to 1
span.quote: For each cell, the procedure learns a set of modality weights, which reflect the relative information content for each data type in that cell.

span.label: the four steps: build a KNN graph per modality, predict within and across modalities, compute per-cell weights, build the WNN graph
span.quote: Our approach consists of four broad steps, as explained in detail below: (1) Constructing independent _k_-nearest neighbor (KNN) graphs for both modalities. (2) Performing within and across-modality prediction (3) Calculating cell-specific modality weights. (4) Calculating a WNN graph.

span.label: spurious edge = a link between cells that share some molecular similarity but are not in a matched molecular state
span.quote: Recent work has clearly demonstrated that KNN-graphs are prone to the formation of spurious edges, which represent links between cells that share some similarity molecular profiles, but are not in a matched molecular state

span.label: sPCA = the transcriptomic projection that maximally captures the structure defined in the WNN graph, rather than the one maximising total variance
span.quote: Instead of seeking to identify a low-dimensional projection that maximizes total variance as in PCA, sPCA identifies a projection of the transcriptome dataset that maximally captures the structure defined in the WNN graph.

span.label: three annotation tiers of increasing granularity: 8, 30 and 57 categories, all carried by every cell
span.quote: To assist in the interpretation of our clusters, we assign each cell three annotations with increasing granularity (level 1, 8 categories; level 2, 30 categories; level 3, 57 categories).

span.label: the weights come from a softmax over the ratio of within-modality to cross-modality prediction affinities
span.quote: We provide a detailed mathematical description for each component of the WNN workflow in the STAR Methods, highlighting three key steps: (1) obtaining within modality and cross-modality predictions, (2) converting these to prediction affinities, based on a cell-specific bandwidth kernel, and (3) calculating modality weights using a softmax transformation.

span.label: the kernel bandwidth is set from the 20 cells with the LOWEST non-zero Jaccard similarity - similar enough to matter, unlikely to be the same state
span.quote: For each cell , we therefore aim to identify the 20 cells in the dataset with the _lowest_ non-zero Jaccard similarity. We expect that these represent cells that exhibit some similarity with cell , but are unlikely to reside in the same molecular state.

span.label: results held across k from 10 to 50, and the protein information did not cost transcriptomic neighbourhood coherence
span.quote: We confirmed that our results were robust to a range of values for _k_ ( Figure S2), and the incorporation of protein information in the WNN graph does not come at the expense of identifying transcriptomically congruent neighborhoods

span.label: the three modality types integrated: gene expression, surface protein abundance, chromatin accessibility
span.quote: Our approach consists of four broad steps, as explained in detail below: (1) Constructing independent _k_-nearest neighbor (KNN) graphs for both modalities. (2) Performing within and across-modality prediction (3) Calculating cell-specific modality weights. (4) Calculating a WNN graph.

span.label: the criteria the method had to meet, declared before it was built: robustness to differences in data quality, support for downstream tasks, and improvement over single-modality analysis
span.quote: To be applied to a range of biological contexts and data types, our strategy must successfully address the following criteria. First, the workflow must be robust to potentially vast differences in data quality between the modalities. Second, integrative multimodal analysis should enable multiple downstream analytical tasks, including visualization, clustering, and the identification of cellular trajectories. Last, and most importantly, simultaneous analysis of multiple modalities should improve on the ability to discover and characterize cell states, compared to independent analyses of each modality when performed separately.

p.note: The full text of this article is not redistributable, so it is not included here. Every tag above carries the exact sentence it was made from, quoted under fair quotation. The article itself is at https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cell.2021.04.048.
